> If there is one feature request that has echoed around Capture One&#8217;s forums for as long as we can remember, it is native Hasselblad support. As of today, that wait is over. Hasselblad and Capture One have announced a partnership that brings native support for Hasselblad&#8217;s medium format RAW files (.3FR) to Capture One, meaning photographers can now import, organise and develop their Hasselblad images directly in the software, with the full toolset of layers, masks, colour editing and precision adjustments at their disposal. Capture One will also be offering a free 7-day trial for users. In the studio we use several rather ancient Hasselblad 500C&#8217;s with digital backs alongside Capture One, a system that we&#8217;ve had in place for well over 10 years and for us it&#8217;s worked personally. > FUJIFILM instax has pulled together a summer travel selection that makes a lot of sense if you like your holiday memories to be physical as well as digital. Rather than focusing on one new product, the line-up brings together instant cameras, hybrid instant cameras, a smartphone printer and decorative film, all aimed at capturing those relaxed, slightly chaotic moments that tend to define a good trip. The most recent model in the selection is the instax mini 13, which feels like the most straightforward travel pick. It has automatic exposure, flash control, Close-up Mode with parallax correction, a selfie mirror and a built-in self-timer. That last feature is especially useful on holiday, because it means you can set the camera down, get everyone into the frame and avoid the usual outstretched-arm group selfie.
